Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexWave Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline, or click the Q&A icon in the webcast platform if attending via computer. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexWave Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We achieved robust subscriber growth and solid revenue execution, which reflects our strong performance in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our NexStream+ service and its positive impact on customer engagement across wireless and broadband bundles. Our investments in 5G Ultra Wideband deployment and converged fiber-to-the-X broadband are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty. Furthermore, we have focused on operational efficiencies in our content and media operations, which has allowed us to maintain profitability while navigating cord-cutting trends. Finally, our strategic focus remains on deleveraging our balance sheet and expanding EBITDA margins through AI-driven optimizations and strategic mix shifts.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $16.2 billion, representing a 6.8% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $5.88 billion, with a margin of 36.3%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $4.2 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion and content slate enhancements.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for NexWave Communications. As we look ahead, I'm pleased to provide our guidance for Q4 2024 and the full fiscal year 2025. This outlook reflects our disciplined execution on key strategic pillars: accelerating 5G Ultra Wideband deployment, scaling our converged fiber-to-the-X broadband footprint, and driving synergies from our recently closed acquisition of StreamForge Media, which bolsters our direct-to-consumer streaming portfolio with premium content bundles akin to those from Disney+ and Peacock.

Let me start with subscribers, where we continue to see robust momentum across our wireless, broadband, and media segments. For Q4, we expect total subscribers to reach 158.2 million, representing net adds of 1.8 million, or 1.1% quarter-over-quarter growth. This compares favorably to our Q3 net adds of 1.5 million and outpaces industry peers like T-Mobile's recent postpaid momentum. Breaking it down: Wireless postpaid phone net adds of 850,000, driven by our 5G standalone core upgrades and promotional pricing on our Unlimited Ultimate plans, which now include bundled access to our NexStream+ SVOD service. We're also seeing early traction in fixed wireless access with 250,000 net adds, targeting underserved rural markets similar to Verizon's FWA ramp-up. Prepaid remains steady at 150,000 adds, bolstered by partnerships with retailers like Walmart. Broadband sees 450,000 net adds in fiber and cable, with ARPU up 2.2% quarter-over-quarter to $68, thanks to gigabit-speed tiers and multi-gig upgrades. Our PON expansion now covers 45% of our footprint, positioning us ahead of Comcast's DOCSIS 4.0 rollout. Media and streaming adds 250,000 net adds to NexStream+, reaching 28 million paid subscribers. Churn improved to 1.8% monthly, below Netflix's sub-2% benchmark, fueled by AI-driven content personalization and exclusive sports rights like regional NFL streaming packages.

ARPU across the board holds steady at $52.50 for wireless and $78 blended for connectivity services, with modest pricing actions offsetting competitive pressures from AT&T's Discovery integration. Turning to revenue: For Q4, we guide to $16.8 billion, up 4.2% quarter-over-quarter and 7.1% year-over-year. This incorporates wireless service revenues of $10.2 billion, up 3.8% year-over-year, with equipment sales at $2.1 billion on strong iPhone 16 demand. Broadband and wireline at $3.4 billion, up 6.5% year-over-year, reflecting 15% year-over-year fiber penetration growth. Media and advertising at $1.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, driven by 20% growth in programmatic ad spend on our connected TV platform, amid the ongoing shift from linear TV, which we expect to decline another 8% portfolio-wide due to cord-cutting trends.

For the full year FY2025, we're raising our guidance to reflect stronger-than-expected 5G adoption and StreamForge synergies. Total subscribers projected at 165.4 million, a 4.5% increase from FY2024's 158.4 million base, implying annualized net adds of 6.9 million. Revenue guidance is now $69.2 billion, up 7.8% year-over-year from our $64.2 billion FY2024 outlook—above consensus estimates and reflecting 200 basis points of outperformance from cost efficiencies. Key FY2025 drivers by region: North America, 85% of revenue, with 5% subscriber growth and 8.5% revenue expansion to $58.8 billion. U.S. wireless market share gains of 50 basis points via spectrum refarming in the C-band post-2023 auction dynamics and edge computing for low-latency gaming and esports. Broadband ARPU uplift from 10G PON trials, targeting 2 million new multi-gig households. Europe, 10% of revenue, 3% subscriber growth to $6.9 billion revenue, navigating regulatory headwinds like the EU's Digital Markets Act but leveraging our Vodafone partnership for 5G roaming efficiencies. Expect 15% year-over-year growth in CTV ad revenues amid linear TV fragmentation. Emerging Markets and LatAm, 5%, high-teens subscriber growth at 12% to $3.5 billion, with prepaid 5G handsets driving 25% ARPU expansion in Brazil and Mexico, countering currency volatility.

Strategically, we're investing $12.5 billion in capex for FY2025, 18% of revenue, focused on 85% 5G coverage, open RAN pilots for opex savings targeting 15% reduction by 2027 akin to Dish Network's model, and AI/ML for churn prediction—already delivering 20 basis points quarterly improvements. EBITDA margins guide to 42-43%, with free cash flow of $11.8 billion supporting $0.65 quarterly dividend and $5 billion in buybacks. Risks include supply chain constraints on sub-6GHz devices, potential FCC spectrum auction delays, and softer ad markets if economic growth moderates below 2.5% GDP. However, our diversified portfolio—blending high-margin connectivity with sticky content—positions us resiliently versus pure-plays like Charter or Warner Bros. Discovery.

Now, let me dive deeper into the performance of our Content and Media segment, which encompasses our direct-to-consumer streaming platform NexStream+—our SVOD and AVOD hybrid service—our portfolio of linear cable networks like NexSports Network and FamilyView Channel, content licensing to third parties, and emerging FAST channels such as NexFree TV. This segment remains a cornerstone of our diversified revenue model, blending high-margin digital growth with the stability of traditional pay TV assets amid ongoing cord-cutting pressures.

Starting with the top line: Content and Media delivered $2.8 billion in revenue for Q3, marking a robust 12% year-over-year increase and 5% sequential growth from Q2. Subscription revenue—primarily from NexStream+ and legacy Pay TV bundles—grew 15% year-over-year to $1.6 billion, driven by paid subscriber net adds and ARPU expansion. This outpaced industry averages, where peers like Disney+ and Paramount+ have seen mid-single-digit sub growth amid price fatigue. Advertising revenue, fueled by our AVOD tier on NexStream+ and FAST inventory, surged 25% year-over-year to $850 million. Upfront ad sales exceeded expectations by 10%, with CPMs up 18% thanks to targeted programmatic buys leveraging our first-party data from 5G-enabled telco integrations. Political ad spend ahead of the U.S. midterms added tailwinds here, similar to what we've seen at Fox and Warner Bros. Discovery. Content licensing and other contributed $350 million, up 8% year-over-year, from syndicating premium IP like our exclusive NFL Sunday Ticket rights and original series to international platforms such as Sky in Europe and JioCinema in India. Adjusted for foreign exchange, organic growth was 11%, reflecting resilience despite a softer linear TV backdrop where U.S. Pay TV households continue to decline at around 5% annually per Nielsen data.

Turning to profitability: We posted adjusted EBITDA of $850 million, a 20% year-over-year increase, with margins expanding 450 basis points to 30.4%. This was our strongest quarterly margin in three years, outpacing Comcast's NBCUniversal at around 28% and reflecting disciplined cost management. Key levers included a 10% reduction in content amortization per hour streamed via better rights recycling—amortizing hits like our 'Empire of Shadows' franchise over 4+ years across windows. Capping new content spend at $1.2 billion for the quarter, flat year-over-year, by prioritizing AI-driven content greenlighting and co-productions. Our proprietary ML models, integrated with AWS SageMaker, improved hit-rate prediction by 22%, reducing flop risk akin to Netflix's algorithmic edge. Operating leverage from scale: Fixed costs like network ops were spread over 18% higher streaming hours viewed. Free cash flow from the segment hit $600 million, up 25%, supporting our $15 billion content capex guidance for FY2024.

Subscriber metrics underscore our dual growth engine of acquisition and retention: Total paid digital subscribers across NexStream+ reached 32.5 million, with 1.2 million net adds in Q3—our best quarter since launch. This included 800,000 from the U.S., boosted by bundling with our 5G mobile plans now at 40% penetration among wireless subs, and 400,000 international adds, led by APAC via partnerships with Singtel and Telstra. Paid households stood at 22 million, with U.S. penetration at 18% of TV households, closing the gap on Hulu's 20% but ahead of Peacock's 15%. Churn held steady at 4.2% monthly, below the SVOD industry average of 5.5% per Antenna data, thanks to personalized recommendations powered by our NexAI engine—boosting retention by 15% for engaged users. ARPU climbed 3% year-over-year to $12.75, driven by tiered pricing with ad-free at $14.99 and ad-supported at $7.99, plus upsells like 4K add-ons. Ex-ad ARPU was $15.20, reflecting premium sports packaging. Legacy Pay TV video subs declined 3% quarter-over-quarter to 18.4 million, in line with industry trends like Charter's 4% drop, but we offset this with $2.50 higher video ARPU from skinny bundles and à la carte sports tiers.

Regionally: North America, 85% of revenue, stellar performance with 14% revenue growth, anchored by U.S. sports rights renewals like NFL and NBA playoffs and NexStream+ originals drawing 2.5 billion hours streamed—up 30% year-over-year. EMEA, 10%, flat revenue at $280 million due to regulatory headwinds on linear carriage fees in the UK and Germany, but digital subs grew 20% via Sky Deutschland bundling. APAC and LatAm, 5%, breakout 35% growth to $140 million, with NexStream+ India hitting 5 million subs on the back of localized Hindi content and Jio 5G synergies—mirroring Disney+ Hotstar's playbook.

Strategically, we're leaning into converged experiences via 5G and edge computing for sub-2-second latency streaming piloted with Ericsson; IP fortress-building with $5 billion in new sports and unscripted commitments, including UEFA Champions League extensions; and AVOD/FAST expansion, targeting 20% of total revenue by 2026 through FAST channels now at 50 million monthly actives. Looking ahead, we guide Q4 segment revenue growth of 10-12% year-over-year, EBITDA margins of 31-33%, and 1 million net adds, with upside from holiday bundling and election ads. Risks remain around content cost inflation and competitive pricing wars, but our telco-media synergies position us uniquely versus pure-plays like Netflix or Roku.

As we wrap up a strong quarter with consolidated revenues up 8% year-over-year to levels supporting our growth trajectory, driven by our 5G fixed wireless access ramp in the U.S. and subscriber growth in our NexStream+ platform, I'd like to spend a few minutes on our balance sheet, specifically our debt levels and leverage profile. Our disciplined capital allocation continues to deliver a robust liquidity position while supporting our strategic investments in next-gen networks and content.

Headline metrics: As of September 30th, our consolidated gross debt stood at $52.3 billion, with net debt—after $2.8 billion in cash and short-term investments—at $49.5 billion. This reflects a modest $1.2 billion increase quarter-over-quarter, primarily from drawdowns on our commercial paper program to fund accelerated 5G mid-band spectrum deployment in Europe, where we successfully bid $1.8 billion in the recent Ofcom 3.6 GHz auction, mirroring the intensity of the FCC's C-band auction earlier this year. On leverage, our net debt to last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA ratio—the key covenant metric under our senior notes and revolving credit facility—came in at 3.2x, down from 3.5x at Q2 end and a full turn lower than 4.2x a year ago. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of deleveraging, fueled by EBITDA growth of 12% LTM to $15.4 billion and free cash flow generation of $4.2 billion in Q3 alone, exceeding our guidance midpoint. For context, this positions us comfortably within our target range of 2.8x to 3.5x, providing ample headroom versus peers like Verizon at 2.9x and AT&T at 3.1x, per their most recent disclosures.

Debt maturity profile remains well-laddered, with no major cliffs until 2026. Short-term debt and commercial paper represent just 8% of the total at $4.2 billion, all at floating rates averaging LIBOR plus 75 bps. Long-term debt is 92%, split roughly 60/40 between fixed and synthetic fixed-rate via our $10 billion interest rate swap book. Our weighted average cost of debt is 4.1%, down 20 basis points year-over-year, thanks to proactive refinancing: in July, we issued $3 billion in 4.25% senior unsecured notes due 2033 at a spread of 125 bps over Treasuries—tighter than our 2022 vintage—using proceeds to tender $2.5 billion of higher-coupon 5.375% notes maturing in 2025. This shaved $45 million in annual interest expense.

Regionally, our leverage profile varies thoughtfully with capex intensity. In North America, where 65% of our EBITDA flows from Verizon-partnered 5G core and Comcast-like cable assets, U.S. segment net debt/EBITDA is a pristine 2.7x, supported by FTTH overbuilds in the Southeast yielding 40% take rates. Europe, at 15% of EBITDA, sits at 4.0x due to regulatory-mandated fiber investments under the EU's Gigabit Society targets—we've deployed 2.5 million premises passed in the UK and Germany YTD—but pro forma for our recent Vodafone Ireland JV, it drops to 3.6x with $800 million in synergies. Latin America, our highest-growth region at 20% EBITDA CAGR, is at 3.8x, reflecting Claro Brasil's $1.2 billion tower monetization earlier this year, which delevered us 0.3x there. Asia-Pacific rounds out at 3.0x, bolstered by our Singtel equity stake and 5G SA trials in India.

Strategically, this leverage discipline underscores our ability to execute in a high-capex industry. Telecom capex remains elevated at 18% of revenues—$5.1 billion in Q3—funding Open RAN pilots with Nokia and Ericsson to cut opex by 15-20% long-term, and media content investments like our $2 billion NexStream+ original slate, rivaling Netflix's output. Yet, with $12.5 billion in liquidity including a fully undrawn $8 billion revolver with covenant headroom of 25% utilization max, we're positioned for opportunistic M&A, such as bolt-on spectrum or regional content libraries amid the streaming consolidation wave—think Warner Bros. Discovery's playbook. Looking forward, we expect Q4 net debt/EBITDA to tick down to 3.1x, assuming $4.8 billion in full-year FCF at the midpoint. Post our pending $4 billion fiber JV in Brazil, pro forma leverage holds at 3.2x. Risks like rising rates are mitigated by 85% fixed-rate debt and our active treasury hedging; we've layered in $5 billion in forward-starting swaps locking sub-4% through 2027. In summary, our balance sheet is rock-solid, enabling us to invest aggressively in 6G R&D and AI-driven personalization while returning 40% of FCF to shareholders via our $3 billion buyback authorization.

Before we open it up to questions, I'd like to provide some color on our forward-looking EBITDA margin guidance, which remains a cornerstone metric for evaluating our operational leverage in this capital-intensive industry. As you know, at NexWave, we report adjusted EBITDA—excluding one-time items like restructuring charges and spectrum auction fees—to give the clearest view of our core profitability from our converged telecom and media operations.

For Q3, we delivered an adjusted EBITDA margin of 36.2%, up 140 basis points year-over-year and ahead of our prior guide. This was driven by strong revenue growth in our 5G mobility segment—up 12% year-over-year on higher postpaid ARPU from premium unlimited plans bundled with our NexStream+ video service—and disciplined OpEx management. We realized $450 million in cost synergies from last year's acquisition of StreamForge Media, akin to the WarnerMedia synergies AT&T realized post-merger, primarily through consolidated content licensing and reduced duplicate ad sales teams.

Looking ahead, we are guiding adjusted EBITDA margins to 37-39% for Q1 2025, implying roughly 100-200 basis points of sequential expansion, and 38-40% for full-year 2025, representing 190-380 basis points of improvement over FY2024's 36.3%. This trajectory reflects continued margin accretion from three key levers: operational efficiencies, strategic revenue mix shifts, and moderating capex intensity. First, on efficiencies: Our AI-powered network orchestration platform, rolled out across 85% of our U.S. footprint this quarter, has reduced energy costs by 18% in 5G core sites—think dynamic spectrum sharing and predictive load balancing, similar to what Ericsson is deploying for Vodafone in Europe. We've also optimized our media delivery stack with edge caching via our partnership with Akamai, cutting CDN latency by 25% and content delivery OpEx by $120 million annually. In fixed broadband, our XGS-PON fiber overbuild in the Midwest—now covering 45% of our 20 million HFC homes—is yielding 15% lower maintenance costs per sub compared to legacy copper.

Regionally, North America remains our margin powerhouse at 41% EBITDA margins, fueled by postpaid phone net adds of 450,000 in Q3 and broadband ARPU expansion to $68 from bundling with ad-supported NexStream+ tiers. Europe, post our 2023 O2 UK acquisition, is tracking at 34% margins but accelerating to 36-38% in FY25 as we harmonize roaming agreements and leverage EU spectrum refarming in the 3.6GHz band. APAC and LatAm are headwinds at 28-30% margins due to competitive pricing pressures from Reliance Jio in India and Claro in Brazil, but we're mitigating via selective 5G Standalone launches and programmatic ad tech upgrades, targeting 32% by year-end.

Strategically, we're shifting mix toward higher-margin services: Wireless now 55% of revenue, up from 52%, with enterprise 5G private networks—like our deal with Ford for connected factories—contributing 22% EBITDA margins. Media, at 25% of revenue, benefits from original content hits like 'NexVerse' driving 8% sub growth to 35 million, while we claw back share in the streaming wars against Netflix and Disney+ through hybrid AVOD/SVOD models. Churn is at a record low 0.9% monthly, thanks to personalized recommendations powered by our Comscore integration. Of course, no guidance is without risks. Headwinds include inflationary pressures on tower leases up 5-7% in 2025 contracts with American Tower and Crown Castle, supply chain delays for Nokia and Qualcomm RAN gear amid U.S.-China tensions, and regulatory overhang from the FCC's looming C-band reimbursement deadlines. Capex will trough at 14% of revenue in FY25, down from 16% in 2024, as 5G mid-band coverage hits 95% in the U.S., freeing cash for deleveraging—our net debt to EBITDA is now 2.6x, targeting 2.3x. In summary, this 38-40% FY25 EBITDA margin guide positions us for industry-leading FCF conversion above 50%, supporting $4.5-5.0 billion in dividends and buybacks. We're uniquely positioned in the telecom-media convergence play, much like how Comcast leverages Peacock with Xfinity, to deliver sustainable 200+ basis points annual margin expansion. As always, forward-looking statements are subject to risks outlined in our 10-K.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Chen with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the subscriber and revenue growth guidance for next quarter and the full year, particularly how you're thinking about regional breakdowns?

Jordan Lee: Certainly, Emily. As I detailed earlier, for Q4 we're guiding to 158.2 million total subscribers with 1.8 million net adds, and $16.8 billion in revenue. For FY2025, that's 165.4 million subs and $69.2 billion in revenue. North America drives the bulk with 5% sub growth and 8.5% revenue to $58.8 billion, Europe at 3% subs to $6.9 billion, and emerging markets with high-teens growth to $3.5 billion. This is underpinned by 5G ramps, fiber expansions, and media synergies, outpacing consensus.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Patel: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for the content and media segment, especially debt management in light of those investments?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, David. Our content and media segment is firing on all cylinders with $2.8 billion in Q3 revenue, up 12% year-over-year, and 30.4% EBITDA margins. Subscribers hit 32.5 million paid digital, with strong bundling. On debt, our net leverage is at a healthy 3.2x, with a laddered profile and $12.5 billion liquidity, giving us flexibility for content commitments like sports rights while deleveraging through FCF.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
